page: Amazon Web Services r5b.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical dedicated cores with two threads per core, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache and instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES. It provides 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, relying on network-attached storage architectures, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent mid-tier multi-core performance alongside slower single-thread throughput. Single-core evaluations, including a Geekbench score of 1133.0, single-threaded gzip compression at 21.9 GB/sec, and stress-ng single-core tests, sit in the lower quartile. Conversely, multi-threaded tasks demonstrate steady capacity, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 14,306.45, a multi-core Geekbench score of 6974.0, and 13.15 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 87.05 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 46.8 GB/sec for uncached writes, delivering solid intermediate throughput for memory-intensive data paths.

The primary resource tradeoff centers on the substantial memory footprint versus moderate per-core compute power and an absence of bundled local disks. Workloads demanding high single-thread clock cycles or low-latency ephemeral disk storage may find the architecture constrained. However, for systems that prioritize high memory density per compute core, the instance represents an efficient infrastructure profile. Amazon Web Services r5b.4xlarge is best suited for in-memory databases, Redis caches, distributed data stores, mid-tier ETL processing, and enterprise application backends that depend on high RAM capacity over raw CPU execution.
